region_site: Interior Alaska (Poker Flat / Fairbanks area), USA
stack_scheme: Daily cross-correlations stacked; reference relative to Jan 2014
depth_sensitivity: Shallow active layer (~0 to few m); deeper-band = deeper thaw; depth-frequency mapping noted
uncertainty_treatment: Correlation-coefficient quality control; Bayesian tomography for spatial maps
best_practice_note: Multi-frequency-band stretching maps thaw-depth progression; interstation distance affects frequency-depth response

target_process: Seasonal freeze-thaw and long-term permafrost degradation
depth_sensitivity: Shallow rock/permafrost lens (site-scale, m to tens of m)
dvv_amplitude: Up to ~3% seasonal (late winter vs late summer); long-term decline ~0.1%/yr
uncertainty_treatment: Comparison with meteorological/borehole records; correlation coefficient
best_practice_note: Single 3-component station enables long-term permafrost monitoring where no station pairs exist

stack_scheme: Daily correlograms from hourly raw data
best_practice_note: High-frequency (>4 Hz) dense small array resolves shallow active-layer freeze-thaw on rock glaciers

region_site: Laurichard (French Alps) and Gugla (Swiss Alps) rock glaciers
depth_sensitivity: ~2-8 m active layer (Gugla ~5 m, Laurichard ~3-4 m)
dvv_amplitude: Resonance higher (stiffer) end of winter, lower in warm periods
best_practice_note: Spectral resonance complements dv/v for shallow elastic freeze-thaw changes in rock glaciers
Noise interferometry tracks ice-sheet seasonal melt where active sources impractical

target_process: Ice-sheet seasonal fluctuation and long-term trends / surface melt-mass change
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal dv/v; <3-month lag vs surface mass change
best_practice_note: Single-station cross-component autocorr enables monitoring at sparse polar stations

target_process: Geothermal reservoir response to operator activities (stimulation/acid job, gas kick)
best_practice_note: Ambient noise revealed aseismic reservoir response invisible to standard microseismic monitoring

target_process: EGS reservoir stimulation / aseismic transient deformation
depth_sensitivity: Coda-wave sensitivity kernels for spatial localization (reservoir depth)
dvv_amplitude: Small transient dv/v co-located with stimulation
best_practice_note: Noise-based imaging localized aseismic deformation from the 2006 Basel stimulation

target_process: Reservoir response to earthquakes and geothermal fluid extraction (poroelastic contraction)
region_site: Salton Sea Geothermal Field, California, USA
coda_window_s: 20 (coda windows -40 to -20 s and 20 to 40 s)
best_practice_note: MWCS on borehole arrays with spectral whitening / 1-bit (MSNoise) resolves production-induced dv/v

target_process: CO2 storage site environmental monitoring (groundwater, ground frost) / CO2-plume attempt
region_site: Ketzin CO2 storage site (CO2SINK), Brandenburg, Germany
depth_sensitivity: Shallow subsurface (upper ~0.5 m); not sensitive to 650 m reservoir
dvv_amplitude: Annual periodic (max ~Nov, min ~Mar); sharp jumps at ground frost
uncertainty_treatment: Weaver et al. (2011) errors; confidence intervals
best_practice_note: Surface arrays sense shallow seasonal/frost effects; deep CO2 plume not resolvable from surface noise

dvv_amplitude: Velocity decrease in months after injection onset
uncertainty_treatment: Seasonal and noise-source effects discussed as caveats
best_practice_note: Reinjection-induced velocity drop attributed to increased water in rock matrix; seasonal correction needed

region_site: Underground coal mine, Upper Silesia, Poland
dvv_amplitude: Temporal dv/v tied to mining advance
best_practice_note: Low-frequency (0.6-1.2 Hz) stretching tracks mining-induced velocity change over short campaigns

target_process: Tailings-dam wall stability / water-content (dv/v vs rainfall)
region_site: Active tailings storage facility (mine), South Africa
dvv_amplitude: dv/v responds to rainfall / water content changes
best_practice_note: Dense geophone array with stretching monitors saturation changes in tailings dam walls

target_process: Open-pit mine slope-failure precursor (subsurface velocity decrease before failure)
stack_scheme: Time-lapse correlations from dense borehole array
dvv_amplitude: Velocity decrease beginning ~12 days before slope failure
best_practice_note: Dense borehole arrays give precursory dv/v decrease days ahead of slope failure
